## An unfamiliar assistant

An unfamiliar system offers to help with your research.

Understanding what produces its answers helps explain both its accomplishments and its limits.


## Two movements

**How the model is created**

Structure, training material, objectives, and parameter updates.

**What happens when it is used**

Current context, learned weights, and generated output.


## Four distinct processes

| Concept | What it describes |
|---|---|
| Architecture | Computational structure |
| Training | Changes to learned parameters |
| Inference | Using the trained model |
| Application | Software that supplies context or executes actions |


## Text and tokens

The system represents text as **tokens**.

A token may be a word, part of a word, or another text unit. Its numerical representation becomes an input to the model.

::: {.source}
Penedo et al. (2024), [FineWeb](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.17557)
:::


## Parameters

Parameters are numerical settings learned during training.

Many settings work together. A single fact need not occupy one identifiable setting.

Model size alone does not establish reliability on your task.


## Attention

Attention combines information from positions in a sequence when building a representation.

The transformer supplies a computational structure for those relationships.

::: {.source}
Vaswani et al. (2017), [Attention Is All You Need](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762)
:::


## Pretraining

1. Supply an example prefix.
2. Predict possible next tokens.
3. Compare predictions with the training continuation.
4. Update parameters.
5. Repeat across many examples.

::: {.source}
Penedo et al. (2024), [FineWeb](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.17557)
:::


## Training material

People select and prepare the material.

Filtering, cleaning, and deduplication influence what the model encounters. FineWeb is one public example of this preparation.

::: {.source}
Penedo et al. (2024), [FineWeb dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceFW/fineweb)
:::


## Broad capabilities

Predicting varied text can develop patterns useful for explanation, translation, and code.

Success on one task still leaves reliability on another task to establish.

::: {.source}
Brown et al. (2020), [Language Models are Few-Shot Learners](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14165)
:::


## The training target

A next-token target comes from the example material.

That material can contain accurate claims, fiction, mistakes, and repeated misconceptions. Prediction alone supplies no universal truth guarantee.

::: {.source}
Lin et al., [TruthfulQA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.07958)
:::


## Base model and assistant

Additional training can shape responses toward instructions and preferred behavior.

Demonstrations and preference feedback are one pathway. Post-training can improve behavior while leaving important limitations.

::: {.source}
Ouyang et al. (2022), [Instruction following with human feedback](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155)
:::


## Inference

Ordinary inference uses learned weights to process the current input.

The context may include instructions, earlier messages, document extracts, and tool results.

Generating a response does not itself update those weights.

::: {.source}
Brown et al. (2020), [Language Models are Few-Shot Learners](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14165)
:::


## The generation loop

1. Process the available context.
2. Predict a distribution over next tokens.
3. Select a token.
4. Add it to the sequence.
5. Continue until a stopping condition.


## Token probability and truth

::: {.large-statement}
A likely continuation can form a false claim.
:::

The predicted probability concerns a token continuation. It is not a factual confidence score for the completed statement.

::: {.source}
Lin et al., [TruthfulQA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.07958)
:::


## A changed answer

| Mechanism | What changes |
|---|---|
| Training | Learned parameters |
| A follow-up correction | Current context |
| Saved application memory | Material supplied to a later call |

A correction can change the next answer without retraining.

::: {.source}
Brown et al. (2020), [Few-shot learning without gradient updates](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14165)
:::


## Fluency and mistakes

Generated text can have the form of a citation or explanation while containing an unsupported claim.

A supplied document can improve available information while still leaving room for misinterpretation.

::: {.source}
Lin et al., [TruthfulQA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.07958)
:::


## Model and application

Producing text that requests a search differs from executing the search.

The application can connect model outputs to tools and repeated calls. Those operations belong to the surrounding system.

::: {.source}
Anthropic, [Building effective agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents)
:::


## The model lifecycle

Architecture defines the structure.

Training changes parameters.

Inference uses those parameters with the current context.

The application can supply information and execute actions.


## A foundation to carry forward

Explain how training differs from inference, and how a model differs from the system around it.

The next teaching materials develop delegation, task specifications, and research practice.
